paper.title_en: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Auxiliary Field Formalism
paper.abstract_en: Causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics can be described in terms of a single auxiliary field, with the theory specified by its potential $W(\varphi)$. We use this formulation to study exact, nonperturbative $T\bar T$-like deformations. The irrelevant deformation rescales the auxiliary potential, whereas the marginal ModMax deformation shifts its argument. The resulting flow equations are obtained directly from the auxiliary-field action. On any domain where $r(ψ)$ is regular and invertible, the irrelevant flow admits an autonomous representation, $\partial_λ\mathcal{L} = X F(r)$, with $r = -T^μ_μ/\sqrt{4X-Y}$ and $X, Y$ denoting the quadratic stress-tensor invariants. We derive the flow function $F(r)$ and show how the auxiliary potential can be reconstructed from it. On an increasing, invertible branch, causality requires $D(r)>1/(1-r)$. A globally single-valued flow function further requires the auxiliary-field ratio $r(ψ)$ to remain one-to-one throughout the physical branch. We also study the relation between the $\varphi$-parity of the auxiliary potential, the evenness of $F(r)$, and the analyticity of the Lagrangian, distinguishing the Maxwell and ModMax vacua. The construction extends to the Hamiltonian formulation, whose coupling flow has the opposite sign. We further express Legendre self-duality, the characteristic cones, and the energy conditions in terms of the flow function, and identify $r=(\varepsilon-p_\perp)/(\varepsilon+p_\perp)$. The framework is illustrated by exact results for generalized Born--Infeld, logarithmic, $q$-deformed, and no-$τ$-maximum electrodynamics.
